sources.title: eCFR, 8 CFR 214.2(o) and (p), Special requirements for admission, extension, and maintenance of status (O and P classifications), current as read (saved from the eCFR renderer API for the same section)
sources.said: An O-1 or O-2 petition may only be filed by a United States employer, a United States agent, or a foreign employer through a United States agent. … Extraordinary ability in the field of arts means distinction. Distinction means a high level of achievement in the field of arts evidenced by a degree of skill and recognition substantially above that ordinarily encountered to the extent that a person described as prominent is renowned, leading, or well-known in the field of arts. … Extraordinary achievement with respect to motion picture and television productions, as commonly defined in the industry, means a very high level of accomplishment in the motion picture or television industry evidenced by a degree of skill and recognition significantly above that ordinarily encountered to the extent that the person is recognized as outstanding, notable, or leading in the motion picture or television field. … ( A ) Consultation with an appropriate U.S. peer group (which could include a person or persons with expertise in the field), labor and/or management organization regarding the nature of the work to be done and the alien's qualifications is mandatory before a petition for an O-1 or O-2 classification can be approved. … In the case of an alien of extraordinary achievement who will be working on a motion picture or television production, consultation shall be made with the appropriate union representing the alien's occupational peers and a management organization in the area of the alien's ability. … approved petition for an alien classified under section 101(a)(15)(O)(i) of the Act shall be valid for a period of time determined by the Director to be necessary to accomplish the event or activity, not to exceed 3 years. … An extension of stay may be authorized in increments of up to 1 year for an O-1 or O-2 beneficiary to continue or complete the same event or activity for which he or she was admitted

sources.title: eCFR, 8 CFR 106.2, Fees (USCIS benefit request fees) (saved from the eCFR renderer API for the same section)
sources.said: ( vii ) Petition for O Nonimmigrant Worker with 1 to 25 named beneficiaries: $1,055. ( viii ) Petition or Application for E, H-3, P, Q, R, or TN Nonimmigrant Worker with 1 to 25 named beneficiaries: $1,015. ( ix ) For small employers and nonprofits as defined in § 106.1(f) , the fees in paragraphs … will be one-half the amount in those paragraphs rounded to the nearest $5 increment. … the Asylum Program Fee must be paid by any petitioner filing a Petition for a Nonimmigrant Worker, Form I-129 under 8 CFR 214.2 , … $600. For petitions: ( i ) Filed by a nonprofit as defined in § 106.1(f) : No fee. ( ii ) Filed by a small employer as defined in § 106.1(f) : $300.

note: Guam is in the Immigration and Nationality Act's United States (8 U.S.C. 1101(a)(38)), so a foreign performer needs the United States' own permission: the O-1 petition (extraordinary ability in the arts; extraordinary achievement for film and television), or the P classification (P-1 groups, P-2 reciprocal exchange, P-3 culturally unique; I-129 fee $1,015, with a labour organisation's consultation, 8 CFR 214.2(p)(7)), which the game doesn't model apart. USCIS's own pages refuse this client; the facts are read in the Code of Federal Regulations (eCFR). No minimum pay or exempt engagement applies to the O-1.
